name: Herod Philip (tetrarch)
title: Tetrarch over Iturea and Trachonitis
summary: Herod Philip was the son of Herod the Great and tetrarch over the northeastern regions of Palestine, including Iturea and Trachonitis. He was known as the most moderate and just of Herod's sons, and founded the city of Caesarea Philippi where Peter confessed Jesus as the Messiah.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as tetrarch in Luke
keyEvents.description: Philip is mentioned as tetrarch over Iturea and Trachonitis when John the Baptist began his ministry, providing a historical timeframe for the events of the gospel.

keyEvents.title: Caesarea Philippi - Peter's confession
keyEvents.description: In the area around Caesarea Philippi, the city that Philip founded and named after himself and Emperor Augustus, Jesus asked his disciples who people said he was, and Peter confessed him as the Messiah.

keyEvents.title: Jesus in Philip's territory
keyEvents.description: Jesus traveled to the villages near Caesarea Philippi, which were located in the tetrarchy of Herod Philip, where he taught his disciples.
